Title: Morocco's new government sworn in under first female prime minister
Article:
RABAT: King Mohammed VI of Morocco on Friday received members of the country's new cabinet, led by Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, and presided over their appointment ceremony at the Royal Palace here.
State-run Maghreb Arabe Presse (MAP) reported that Fatima Ezzahra is the first Moroccan woman to hold the country's top government post.
She heads a new government formed by a four-party coalition comprising her Authenticity and Modernity Party, the Istiqlal Party, the Socialist Union of Popular Forces, and the Party of Progress and Socialism.
The new government includes seven women, including Fatima Ezzahra, compared with six in the previous government led by Aziz Akhannouch.
The new government comprises 32 members, including ministers and ministers-delegate, according to official figures.
Abdelouafi Laftit kept his post as interior minister, alongside Nasser Bourita as foreign minister, Abdellatif Ouahbi as justice minister and Ahmed Toufiq as minister of Islamic affairs and endowments.
The new cabinet also established a Ministry of Artificial Intelligence, Digital Transformation and Administrative Reform, headed by Ahmed Rahhou.
On Monday, the Authenticity and Modernity Party, Istiqlal Party, Socialist Union of Popular Forces and Party of Progress and Socialism announced in a joint statement that they had formed the governing majority following the conclusion of the second round of consultations on forming a government, which began on Sept. 30.
On Sept. 29, King Mohammed VI tasked Fatima Ezzahra with forming a government after her party, the Authenticity and Modernity Party, came first in the Sept. 23 elections with 97 seats.

Title: Johor leads unhealthy air quality readings, followed by Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor and Selangor remain the states worst affected by haze, with 24 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recording unhealthy levels as of 8.30am today.
Data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed eight stations in Johor and five in Selangor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
Pasir Gudang recorded the highest API reading in Johor at 198, followed by Larkin (178), Pengerang (175), Kota Tinggi (173), Batu Pahat (170), Tangkak (167), Segamat (160), and Kluang (159).
In Selangor, Johan Setia logged the highest reading at 172, followed by Klang (171), Petaling Jaya (169), Shah Alam (168), and Banting (152).
In the Federal Territories, Putrajaya recorded an unhealthy reading of 162, while Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur registered 161 and 158, respectively.
In Negri Sembilan, Nilai posted a reading of 174, followed by Seremban (171) and Port Dickson (158).
Melaka saw unhealthy air quality in three areas: Bandaraya Melaka (169), Bukit Rambai (166), and Alor Gajah (165).
In Sabah, Sandakan and Tawau registered unhealthy levels at 155 and 151, respectively.
Meanwhile, 43 stations nationwide recorded moderate air quality.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and above 300, hazardous.

Title: UN Security Council holds 6th straw poll on secretary-general candidates
Article:
NEW YORK: The UN Security Council on Friday held its sixth straw poll on candidates vying to become the next UN secretary-general, reported Xinhua.
"The sixth round of straw polls has taken place," said Aglaia Balta, Greece's permanent representative to the United Nations, whose country holds the rotating presidency of the Security Council for the month of October.
Each candidate will be informed of the results through the permanent representatives of nominating member states.
The president of the UN General Assembly will also be informed that the poll has been conducted, Balta told reporters after the secret vote.
Security Council straw polls on secretary-general candidates are informal closed-door ballots used to determine the viability of the candidates. Their results are not officially released.
Through the polls, the Security Council selects a candidate to recommend to the General Assembly for appointment as the next UN secretary-general.
Security Council members were believed to receive one ballot per candidate, containing the candidate's name followed by three options: "encouraged," "discouraged" and "no opinion expressed."
To win the Security Council's recommendation, a candidate needs to gain at least nine "encouraged" votes and no "discouraged" votes from any of the five permanent members of the council.
[[nid:1557241]]
Seven candidates remain in the race: Ivonne A-Baki, a former Ecuadorian minister and diplomat; Maria Fernanda Espinosa, a former president of the UN General Assembly and former foreign minister and defense minister of Ecuador; Rafael Grossi of Argentina, current director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency; Rebeca Grynspan, a former vice president of Costa Rica and current secretary-general of the UN Conference on Trade and Development; Olara Otunnu of Uganda, a former UN under-secretary-general; Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, Guyana's permanent representative to the United Nations; Macky Sall, a former president of Senegal.
Current UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' term expires at the end of this year. His successor is scheduled to take office on Jan 1, 2027. — BERNAMA

Title: ISF venturing into NRW for next growth wave [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Less than a year after its debut on Bursa Malaysia, ISF Group Bhd is looking to further diversify its revenue base with recurring income sources from partnerships with states water authority to reduce non-revenue water (NRW).
While the company has built its recent growth momentum by riding the data centre boom across Malaysia, its management is cultivating its next major growth drive through cutting-edge technology partnerships to deliver comprehensive NRW solutions.
"ISF is looking at elevating our position to public infra, like projects from PAAB (Perbadanan Aset Air Bhd), and projects from state governments," said its group managing director Jeff Ai Boon Chen in an exclusive interview with Business Times.
To execute this vision, the company is finalising a strategic joint venture with a Hong Kong-listed subsidiary of a major Chinese water firm to introduce smart meters and AI-driven monitoring software to local state water authorities.
"So, instead of working conventionally, like we just purchase technology from them, we will be working as joint venture partners, in which each company will own a stake in this subsidiary. Because we are looking at the long term, rather than every time we need one-off technology," said Ai.
He added that in China, the water supply authority can control the flow of water in each house, through digital sensors and valves in the smart meters, to ensure commercial NRWs - customers not paying their water bills - are addressed there.
ISF's competitive edge lies in acting as the local executor and coordinator, filling the gap where foreign technology suppliers struggle with local deployment and state authorities lack full operational capability.
"So, the technology, the manufacturing and everything will be handled by them. So, there won't be any conflict of interest. So, that is why we work as partners... But, with this joint venture, ISF will act as a so-called party to coordinate everything.
"We execute the work, pipe replacement, everything we can do ourselves," said Ai.
ISF is already in negotiations with a state government in the northern peninsular to implement the NRW management system.
The company is currently funding a proof of concept (POC) to demonstrate the efficacy of this system, paving the way for long-term recurring revenue models, he said.
The commercial arrangements that ISF is looking at with the state's water authority is either through profit sharing or one-off project costs that come with operation and maintenance (O&M) contracts, said Ai.
"But it is a long-term thing that we are looking at because we need to have recurrent income rather than purely doing projects. What we are doing now is actually preparing for the next wave (to ride on).
"Hopefully, by maybe the third or fourth quarter of 2027, there will be concrete things. So, the next growth story will begin," he said.
Riding the data centre wave while maintaining strategic diversification
While NRW technology represents the future horizon, data centre (DC) projects serve as ISF's immediate revenue engine.
The company's involvement in the sector dates back nearly a decade, giving it an early-mover advantage over competitors.
Riding on the DC construction wave, ISF's net profits in the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY25) surged 163 per cent to RM25.34 million, compared with RM9.64 million in the preceding financial year.
In the first six months of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY26), ISF reported net profits of RM12.5 million, on the back of RM57.6 million in revenue.
The six-month revenue was 58.4 per cent of FY25's total, and already exceeded FY24's revenue of RM54.67 million.
DC works have grown substantially as a share of overall revenue, but management remains steadfast in diversifying across multiple asset classes to protect the business against cyclical shifts.
"So, over the years, it has increased from maybe 10 to 15 percent to I think exceeding 50 percent revenue for FY25. So, we are still looking at revenue from DC jobs also exceeding 50 percent for FY26," said Ai.
However, DC plumbing and piping is only one of the capabilities that ISF could do.
The group is also involved in industrial and commercial assets piping contracts, as well as water distribution and sewerage.
"We consistently tell the public that we are a diversified plumbing contractor. So, every cycle is a good cycle for ISF because you know, we do everything. We are not telling you we can only do DC.
"We still maintain 15 per cent for residential, commercial, industrial and other stuff. So, maybe next year, when the market share of DCs eventually gets smaller, maybe slowly to 30 per cent, our other segments will slightly increase to between 30 and 40 per cent (of revenue)," said Ai.
Looking ahead, ISF anticipates a temporary stabilisation in DC tendering as the industry pivots to execution, opening up space for healthcare and medical infrastructure projects.
"I foresee there will be a bit of a slowdown of the DC standards starting from the first or second quarter of next year. Now is the awarding period, a lot of announcements. So, next year will be the so-called execution year."
"I am looking at next year, maybe we will shift more on the industrial and also on the hospitals, healthcare kind of things. At the end of next year, there will be quite a number of hospitals to be built," said AI.
Institutional Backing Through IPO
ISF's shift from a private entity to a publicly listed company was guided by a desire to install strong corporate governance and attract top professional talent rather than maintaining a strict family dynasty, said AI.
"So, in order for good talent to get into the business, of course, we need to be transparent. Since day one, we are not looking at turning ISF into a family legacy. I've never had the mindset that I'm going to pass ISF down to my children.
"Because my initial intention is very simple. I look at other companies, let's say Hilton. We don't even know who the boss is, but everything is operating smoothly," said Ai.
This institutional transparency brought by being a publicly-listed company has attracted major fund managers, collectively holding more than 20 per cent of ISF's share base.
Despite interest from existing institutional investors to increase their stakes, ISF is adequately capitalised with existing proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO) and internally generated cash to fund its robust tender pipeline.
"Currently, we still have some cash reserves from the IPO. So far, we are still okay with using our existing cash to support our growth," said Ai.
According to its 2025 annual report, institutional investors of ISF include Kumpulan Sentiasa Cemerlang Sdn Bhd, Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd, Hong Leong Dana Makmur, KAF Tactical Fund and AIA Public Takaful Bhd.
However, none of the institutions are substantial shareholders of ISF.
ISF raised RM61.15 million from its IPO in January, with nearly two-third of the proceeds reserved for purchasing operational materials and paying subcontractors.
About 19 per cent is allocated to establish and expand operational facilities, including a new head office at its home base in Johor, and new regional offices in Selangor or Negri Sembilan, and Penang.
A portion of the capital raised is further allocated toward expanding its fleet of heavy machinery and recruiting additional personnel.
Funds from the IPO proceeds and its internally-generated cash are currently enough for its current tender book balance of approximately RM600 million, said Ai.
Historically, ISF managed to secure between 20 and 30 per cent of its tender book as orders.
"So, we are still looking at an annual replenishment of RM150 million per year for new wins," he said.
Defending Profit Margins
ISF commands strong profit margins by maintaining direct operational control, capturing economies of scale, and reducing dependency on third-party subcontractors. As of 6M FY26, ISF's gross margin stood at 30.89 per cent.
The group is looking at improving its gross margins over the next two years, said Ai.
"So, actually, why we are able to command good margins is because of the economy of scale. We are one of the largest plumbing contractors, so we are able to have a better command on the pricing with the suppliers.
"Secondly, we do a lot of things in-house," he said.
To tackle localised labour constraints particularly in Johor where labor competition with Singapore is intense, ISF utilises independent subcontractors strictly for supplemental labour while retaining full ownership of equipment and management.
ISF remains unthreatened by foreign entrants or Chinese investments, as those entities typically operate in closed, in-house ecosystems that fall outside its core target client base.
While the group has been registering strong profit growth, ISF has not declared a dividend, as it prioritises reinvesting earnings into expansions.
The group does not have a dividend policy at the moment.
"We do not have a formal policy on issuing dividends, because, as you can see, our growth is exponential. So, we need to conserve quite substantial cash with us to support our projects," said Ai.
As of Oct 15, ISF's share price appreciated more than 65 per cent to 80 sen apiece, valuing the group at RM795 million.

Title: Malaysia's GDP growth beats expectations [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's third-quarter 2026 advance gross domestic product (GDP) estimate of 5.3 per cent is a positive surprise despite external shocks, particularly the ongoing US-Iran conflict, economists said.
They told Business Times that while growth moderated from six per cent in the preceding quarter, the slowdown did not necessarily signal a broad-based loss of economic momentum.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said proactive government measures, including targeted fuel subsidies through MyKad introduced last year, had helped cushion the economy against external shocks.
Petroliam Nasional Bhd's efforts to secure fuel supplies from outside the Strait of Hormuz also helped minimise disruptions to domestic economic activity, he added.
Foreign investor interest in Malaysia and stronger demand for technology-related sectors had also supported growth, while full employment and relatively contained inflation helped sustain consumer spending.
"Overall, it is a positive surprise and it looks like the growth numbers could be surprised on the upside with the prevailing GDP growth projection currently standing between 4.8 per cent to 5.3 per cent," the economist said.
He added that growth of 5.3 per cent would put Malaysia's economy above its estimated trend growth rate of around 4.7 per cent.
According to the advance estimate released by the Statistics Department today, Malaysia's GDP is estimated to have grown 5.3 per cent in Q3, slightly higher than the 5.2 per cent recorded in the corresponding period last year.
Bank Negara Malaysia is scheduled to release the official Q3 GDP figures on Nov 18.
Growth eased from six per cent in the preceding quarter, with all economic sectors expanding except mining and quarrying.
For the first nine months of 2026, the economy grew 5.5 per cent, compared with 4.8 per cent in the same period last year.
The services sector remained the main growth driver, expanding 5.4 per cent, supported by wholesale and retail trade, information and communication, as well as finance and insurance activities.
Manufacturing growth accelerated to 7.5 per cent from 7.3 per cent in the preceding quarter, driven by export-oriented industries, particularly electrical, electronic and optical products, as well as petroleum, chemicals, rubber and plastics products.
Construction growth eased to six per cent from 6.5 per cent, supported by non-residential projects, particularly data centres, and specialised construction works.
The agriculture sector rebounded 1.3 per cent after contracting 3.7 per cent in the preceding quarter, driven by oil palm and livestock activities.
In contrast, mining and quarrying contracted 4.9 per cent, reversing the 9.2 per cent expansion recorded in the second quarter, following a decline in crude oil and condensate production.
Despite the expansion, Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said Malaysia should remain mindful of risks stemming from its exposure to global trade and the current AI investment cycle.
He said softer global technology spending could weigh on semiconductor exports, manufacturing activity and data centre investments.
Higher oil prices could raise businesses' operating costs and further erode household purchasing power.
"Another concern is whether domestic consumption can remain strong if wages fail to keep pace with living costs.
"Malaysia should therefore strengthen domestic economic resilience by improving productivity, supporting small and medium enterprises, attracting higher-value investments and developing new export markets.
"The priority is not simply to maintain headline growth, but to ensure that growth is broad-based and sustainable, so the economy can withstand external shocks without placing excessive pressure on households or public finances," Idham said.
He said Malaysia remains on a relatively solid growth trajectory, but sustaining this momentum will depend on domestic demand, the quality of investments and efforts to diversify the economy's growth drivers.

Title: Pas' move to prioritise Umno, BN signals intent, not electoral realignment, says analyst
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas' decision to prioritise Umno and Barisan Nasional in negotiations for the next general election signals a willingness to explore closer cooperation, but does not yet indicate a new electoral alliance is taking shape, says a political analyst.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Tawfik Yaakub said the decision by Pas' Syura Council gave the party's central leadership room to pursue talks with Umno and BN while potentially strengthening its bargaining position with other political parties.
"This is a meaningful signal of strategic intent, but it is not yet evidence of a settled electoral realignment.
"Whether it represents a genuine shift will depend on whether both sides move from statements to concrete discussions on seats, leadership and a shared policy platform," he said.
Yesterday, Pas spiritual leader Datuk Hashim Jasin said the party would prioritise Umno and BN over other political parties in
negotiations for the next general election
.
Hashim said the decision was made at a recent Syura Council meeting he chaired, which mandated the party's central leadership to negotiate with any party, with Umno given priority.
He said the council recognised that bringing Pas and Umno together would not be easy and that the opportunity should be fully utilised.
Hashim added that Pas was more comfortable cooperating with Umno than with other parties, noting that the people wanted unity between the two Malay-Muslim parties.
He also said the unity must be built on the interests of the Malays and Islam rather than political considerations.
Asked whether the decision could create unease within Perikatan Nasional, Tawfik said it could, particularly if Umno was treated as Pas's preferred partner without clear consultation with other component parties.
"The challenge for Pas will be to pursue talks with Umno without weakening trust among its existing partners," he said.
On the possibility of a renewed Pas-Umno arrangement, Tawfik said such cooperation was possible but would require substantial compromises to remain viable.
"Both parties would need to reach agreement on seat allocation, candidate selection, leadership arrangements and the terms of any post-election cooperation, while addressing longstanding issues of trust and political rivalry.
"They would also need to demonstrate that the partnership was based on more than a temporary electoral bargain," he said.
Tawfik said cooperation between the two parties could reduce competition for Malay-Muslim votes in certain constituencies, but would not automatically consolidate those voters behind a single alliance.
"Supporters may have different priorities and may not accept every compromise made by their party leadership," he said.
He added that the arrangement could also create divisions within the parties and raise questions among BN's non-Malay partners and voters about the coalition's political direction.
On which party stood to gain more from the proposed cooperation, Tawfik said Pas could gain more immediate political leverage by using the prospect of an alliance to strengthen its negotiating position.
Umno, meanwhile, could benefit from access to Pas's support base and an opportunity to rebuild its political relevance, although it risked being perceived as the junior partner.
"The eventual balance of gains will depend on the seat-sharing formula, the leadership arrangement and each party's ability to retain its own identity and supporters," he said.

Title: N. Korea tests AI-assisted torpedo system: KCNA
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea has tested a "new-type" precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance, state news agency KCNA reported early Saturday.
The underwater test-fire of the "super-speed" Zam-2.0 system took place on Thursday "to confirm the successful technical updating" of the weapon, the Korean Central News Agency said.
"AI technology was applied to the target detection and the guidance function of the new-type super-speed precisely guided torpedo," KCNA said.
Earlier this month, North Korea announced that it had proceeded with the AI-assisted launch of an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
In September, the country's leader Kim Jong Un emphasised the need to raise "the level of artificial intelligence" in the country's weapons systems.
Analysts have said North Korea could be rapidly advancing its missile technology with Russian military support in exchange for sending troops to support its war against Ukraine.

Title: Kenya records third Ebola case in the country
Article:
NAIROBI: Kenya has recorded its third case of Ebola, a close relative of the country's first two Ebola cases, the health ministry said on Friday.
The country had not reported a single case of the contagious virus until last week, after a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) died after returning to Kenya.
Just over a week later a second man, a relative of the first, also tested positive for the virus while in quarantine.
The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May. The deadly disease has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.
The 65-year-old woman was a "primary contact and a close relative of the first and second cases", the ministry said in a statement, adding that she had been in quarantine since October 6.
After developing symptoms, including "fever, sore throat and malaise", she was isolated and tested positive for the virus.
The ministry emphasised that the risk to the public "remains low" and there was "no evidence of community transmission."
It said of 130 contacts, 127 had been traced and were in quarantine, with efforts "ongoing to trace and quarantine the three remaining contacts."
On Wednesday, the ministry confirmed its second case, a 39-year-old relative of the first victim, stating he was in isolation and there was "no evidence" of any large-scale transmission of the virus.
The country has never previously reported a case.
Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 people infected, almost all of whom had travelled from the neighbouring DRC, and two deaths, before being declared Ebola-free in August.
Kenya's first victim was a national, who has not been named but was referred to as a 40-year-old businessman.
He fell ill around a month ago and had been treated in the DRC, before travelling overland to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, and flying into Nairobi on October 3.
He was hospitalised in Nairobi but died on October 5, according to Health Minister Aden Duale.
According to Congolese health authorities, the outbreak has infected 9,066 people so far and caused 4,381 deaths since the emergence in the DRC of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment.

Title: 'Great hero' praised for saving lives in Oregon school shooting
Article:
BEND, United States: The "hero" who shot dead a teenage gunman after he had already killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school was named Friday, as the US entered a familiar – and likely fruitless – debate about gun control in the wake of the latest tragedy.
Kaylub Giamanco raced into Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, after the shooter, identified by local media as 16-year-old John J. Griffin II, blasted his way through locked doors and opened fire on youngsters.
Kyle Giamanco said 36-year-old Kaylub, who has two children at the school, was driving home for his lunch break on Thursday when he heard gunshots and saw Griffin going into the special education room of the school.
Kaylub Giamanco has a permit to carry a concealed weapon, his brother told NBC, adding that he was having difficulty processing events at the moment and feels guilty that he did not save more people.
A woman identified as his mother told the local Fox affiliate she was "very proud" and that her son was "an absolute hero" before she read a prepared statement.
"He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," she said.
US President Donald Trump hailed Giamanco as a "great hero."
"As bad as it was, we had a great hero that went in and did the business," Trump told journalists. "It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it."
On Friday, the small city in the US northwest was struggling to come to terms with a tragedy that took the lives of children aged five, eight and 11, as well as a teacher, the latest victims of America's epidemic of gun violence that all-too-frequently afflicts the nation's schools.
Streets were quiet in an area known for its natural beauty, with hiking trails and ski pistes nearby that attract tens of thousands of visitors every year.
Kristen Vanetsky, 52, told AFP she was in shock over the shooting at her grandson's school.
"My grandson should be in his classroom, with all of his friends," she said.
"Everybody should be in there learning, having fun, looking forward to their weekend, and it's just vacant," she said. "There's nothing. Even the birds are not here."
GUN VIOLENCE
Even as the city tried to process the tragic events, the familiar contours of an argument that plays out after every school shooting in the US began to harden.
The politically powerful National Rifle Association (NRA) praised the then-unidentified bystander who stepped in to prevent even greater loss of life.
"Yesterday's terrible act of violence in Oregon serves as another reminder of the importance of a law-abiding armed citizenry," the NRA said in a post on X.
The man's actions "exemplify the heroism of everyday citizens who are prepared and ready to respond when innocent lives are on the line," it added.
The NRA has invested millions of dollars campaigning for gun rights and supporting politicians who block the limits on ownership that the vast majority of Americans support.
Gun control advocates again lamented the ready availability of weaponry in a country where the number of gun-related deaths far outpaces most of the developed world.
"America's gun violence crisis is killing our babies. Enough is enough," gun-control group GIFFORDS said on X.
More than 360 mass shootings have been recorded across the United States this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines them as incidents in which at least four people are shot, excluding the gunman.
LONG GUN
Griffin's neighbours told AFP they had seen his mother taken away from the house she shared with the suspect on Thursday afternoon in a police patrol car.
That woman, Shauntai May Nickerson, was seen on Friday smoking a cigarette on the porch outside of her apartment and crying.
"If I could have prevented this, I would have," a tearful Nickerson said, according to The New York Times.

Title: Transport infrastructure under siege: Cable thieves putting commuters at risk
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cable thieves continue to target transport infrastructure, with recent incidents involving the Kajang MRT Line and the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) highlighting security concerns.
In the latest incident, thieves cut about 100m  of cable between Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara stations early yesterday.
They abandoned it when auxiliary police and Prasarana personnel approached.
The thieves are believed to have rolled up the cables and left them aside for later collection.
Separately, PLUS Malaysia Bhd said its personnel and police had foiled a suspected cable theft attempt along the NKVE, leading to a suspect's arrest.
Photographs by PLUS  showed what appeared to be cutting equipment, including a cordless power tool, a hacksaw, a hand saw and a toolbox, beside a concrete roadside barrier.
Another photograph showed damaged cables along a highway embankment, with sections exposed and out of place.
The incidents highlight the threat of cable theft to both railway and highway infrastructure.
MRT SERVICES DISRUPTED
The attempted theft on the Kajang MRT Line was detected  about 5.30am after someone entered the track area between Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara stations.
Rapid KL said power to the affected section was temporarily cut in line with safety procedures.
The power cut allowed auxiliary police to inspect the area and search for suspects while protecting passengers, staff and railway facilities.
Power was restored at 6.32am after the  checks were completed.
Rapid KL provided alternative services during the disruption so passengers could continue their journeys.
The company said cable theft could disrupt train services and endanger passengers and staff.
A police report was lodged at Brickfields  police headquarters.
PLUS FOILS  CABLE THEFT
PLUS said its personnel and police had arrested a suspect in an alleged cable theft attempt along the NKVE. The suspect was handed over to police at Sentul  police headquarters
PLUS did not disclose when the operation took place or how much cable was involved.
Its photographs showed the scene and equipment suspected of being used in the theft.
PLUS said the theft or damage of highway facilities, including cables, safety barriers and road signs, could pose serious risks.
Such theft and damage could endanger motorists and affect highway safety systems.
The incidents have renewed concerns about cable theft syndicates targeting railway infrastructure using  sophisticated methods.
Prasarana previously told the
New Straits Times
that cable thieves were exploiting hidden spaces in the concrete structures supporting elevated MRT tracks.
They have used openings in viaducts, nearby billboards and concealed spaces beneath elevated tracks to access the cables.
Prasarana had identified the area around Phileo Damansara as vulnerable because of its terrain and several  entry points.
Prasarana has increased auxiliary police patrols and introduced canine units, better surveillance and additional physical barriers.
Prasarana previously said cable theft had cost it RM20.6 million over three years.
Cases rose from 42 in 2024 to 72 last year.
The operator said  that 43 per cent of the 72 cable theft cases recorded last year involved access through concrete piers and viaduct structures.
Other access methods included breaches in perimeter fencing, hillside approaches and  billboards.
The Kajang MRT Line is about 48km long and has 1,394 piers. The Putrajaya MRT Line is 68km long, with 1,265 piers.

Title: NST CRIME WATCH: Fatal BYD Seal crash, police chase and cable theft arrests [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A five-year-old girl was killed in a six-vehicle crash involving a BYD Seal along Jalan Kuching on Oct 10, in one of the week's most tragic incidents.
The girl was in the
rear passenger seat of a Perodua Bezza
driven by her 30-year-old father when the crash occurred as traffic moved slowly from the city centre towards Segambut.
Police said initial investigations found that the BYD Seal had rear-ended the Bezza, triggering a chain collision involving a Yamaha 135LC motorcycle and three other cars – a Nissan Almera, Toyota Alphard and Perodua Myvi.
The girl suffered severe head injuries and died en route to Hospital Kuala Lumpur. Her father injured his right hand, while the 33-year-old motorcyclist suffered head injuries.
The 24-year-old BYD Seal driver was admitted to a private hospital in Damansara for concussion treatment.
Here are the week's other major crime stories:
DRAMATIC POLICE CHASE IN WANGSA MAJU
Two men were
arrested after a police chase
from Bukit Antarabangsa to Setiawangsa on Oct 11. Videos of the pursuit and members of the public helping police went viral on social media.
[[nid:1557193]]
Police pursued the suspects in an Isuzu D-Max pickup truck along Jalan Wangsa 5 in Bukit Antarabangsa towards the Middle Ring Road 2 before intercepting the vehicle at the junction of Jalan Jelatek and Jalan Taman Setiawangsa, near a petrol station.
A search of the vehicle uncovered a parang, a sickle, equipment believed to have been used to steal cables, including a manhole cover opener, and substances suspected to be drugs.
Videos showed the suspects trying to flee after their vehicle collided with other vehicles, while members of the public helped police apprehend them.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant, as well as provisions on offensive weapons and drug possession.
29 NABBED FOR PROMOTING UNLAWFUL ORGANISATIONS ONLINE
Police arrested 29 men, including a foreigner, in a nationwide operation targeting those suspected of
promoting unlawful organisations
on social media.
Codenamed Ops Mega TikTok 2026, the operation was conducted from Oct 10 to 12 by Bukit Aman's Criminal Investigation Department (CID), with the cooperation of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
[[nid:1557192]]
Bukit Aman CID director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects, aged 18 to 49, were detained in coordinated operations involving 11 police contingents across Selangor, Johor, Pahang, Penang, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Negri Sembilan, Kedah, Melaka, Sabah and Sarawak.
Police are also probing possible links between the suspects and other criminal activities, amid concerns over the use of social media to promote unlawful organisations.
14 ARRESTED IN CABLE THEFT CRACKDOWN
Police arrested
14 suspects linked to cable thefts
in Selangor, Kedah, Melaka and Negri Sembilan.
The arrests came amid concerns over syndicates targeting telecommunications, railway and electrical infrastructure, with recent thefts disrupting essential services.
[[nid:1557191]]
Crime experts have called for tougher action against scrap metal dealers suspected of buying stolen cables, warning that the illegal resale market fuels theft.
They said enforcement should target not only thieves but also the buyers and middlemen behind the trade.
5 MALAYSIANS HELD IN TOKYO OVER 5KG COCAINE HAUL
Five Malaysians have been
arrested in Tokyo for smuggling 5kg of cocaine,
prompting Malaysian border authorities to warn travellers against carrying luggage or parcels for others overseas.
Malaysian police will send an investigation team to Japan following the arrests.
[[nid:1557190]]
Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team would gather information about the arrests, including details of local and international drug syndicate networks.
He said Japanese authorities were tracing the cocaine's source and identifying those behind the smuggling attempt, including members of international drug trafficking networks.
POLICE PROBE ASSAULT, VANDALISM LINKED TO TASEK BERA OPERATION
Police are looking for a suspect who allegedly damaged a pickup truck and assaulted a man in Kampung Kuala Serting, Bera.
The suspect smashed a Toyota Hilux's side mirror, punched a man on the shoulder and fled on foot.
Police believe the incident was linked to a land enforcement operation by the Pahang State Enforcement Unit (UPNP) at the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve.
The UPNP and several other agencies are remeasuring the forest reserve to curb encroachment.
In recent weeks, several villagers have reportedly been arrested for obstructing enforcement personnel. Threats have also allegedly been made to stop the operation.
CUSTOMS OFFICER MURDERED, HUSBAND, ARRESTED
Police believe a marital dispute led to the
death of a 35-year-old Customs officer,
who was allegedly murdered by her husband in a public housing complex in Nilai on Thursday.
Initial checks indicated that the victim had been stabbed, with the weapon recovered at the scene.
The husband surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor.
The victim was a Customs officer who transferred to the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) service scheme on July 1.

Title: NST COURT WATCH: School tragedies, fatal crashes and child abuse [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The deaths of young people featured prominently in court proceedings this week, from the murder of a 16-year-old girl by her classmate to a student killed in a crash on school grounds and a five-year-old girl killed in a six-vehicle pile-up.
In Batu Pahat, a Form 4 student was charged with murdering his classmate, Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, at their school in Yong Peng.
In Kota Baru, a teacher claimed trial to negligence charges over a crash that killed a Form 1 student and injured another. In Kuala Lumpur, a 24-year-old motorist denied causing five-year-old Asiah Ahmad Syahir's death through reckless driving.
Two other children's deaths also featured in court proceedings.
In Kota Kinabalu, the inquest into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir concluded witness testimony after hearing from 83 witnesses.
In Johor Baru, the High Court detailed the abuse suffered by a three-year-old boy who died after being mistreated by a man entrusted with his care.
Elsewhere, a lorry driver claimed trial to driving under the influence of drugs in a 12-vehicle pile-up in Shah Alam, while former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak failed in his bid to suspend his 15-year jail sentence and RM11.4 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case.
Perikatan Nasional (PN) also obtained permission to challenge the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) decision to suspend its activities, but the High Court rejected its application for an interim stay.
Here are some of the week's major court cases and developments.
TEENAGER CHARGED WITH MURDERING CLASSMATE
A 16-year-old Form 4 student was charged with murdering his classmate, Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, at the Batu Pahat magistrate's court.
The accused nodded as magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno read out the charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code during closed-door proceedings.
[[nid:1557206]]
He was accused of murdering Irene Sofiya at the hall of SMK Dato' Seth in Yong Peng between 2.30pm and 4pm on Oct 3.
Irene Sofiya's family members and members of the public gathered at the court complex to follow the proceedings.
She was found lying in the school hall with bloodstains on her body and bruises that appeared consistent with being beaten.
BYD SEAL DRIVER CHARGED OVER GIRL'S DEATH
The parents of five-year-old Asiah Ahmad Syahir sat in the last row of the public gallery at the Kuala Lumpur magistrate's court as the man accused of causing their daughter's death in a six-vehicle crash claimed trial.
[[nid:1557205]]
Raeven Goh, 24, pleaded not guilty to three traffic offences, including causing Asiah's death through reckless driving along Jalan Kuching on Oct 10.
The bank sales manager also denied driving in a manner that endangered other road users and failing to stop and report the accident.
The court granted him bail of RM36,000 with one surety, ordered him to surrender his passport and suspended his driving licence pending disposal of the case.
TEACHER CHARGED OVER STUDENT'S DEATH AT SCHOOL
A 57-year-old teacher, Sakinah Ismail, pleaded not guilty at the Kota Baru magistrate's court to two charges involving negligence that caused a Form 1 student's death and injured another at SMK Tanjong Mas.
[[nid:1557204]]
Sakinah was accused of driving a car that struck the two students within the school compound in April.
The case has drawn attention to student safety on school grounds.
LORRY DRIVER CLAIMS TRIAL OVER 12-VEHICLE PILE-UP
Lorry driver C. Agilan, 51, pleaded not guilty at the Shah Alam magistrate's court to driving under the influence of drugs in a 12-vehicle crash that injured four people.
[[nid:1557203]]
He was accused of driving a 10-tonne lorry under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamine along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari in Alam Budiman on Oct 9.
The crash, involving 11 other vehicles at a traffic light junction, was captured on video and widely shared on social media.
Agilan also faced a separate charge of self-administering the drugs. His driving licence was suspended pending disposal of the case.
HIGH COURT DETAILS ABUSE OF THREE-YEAR-OLD BOY
The Johor Baru High Court detailed the abuse suffered by a three-year-old boy at the hands of a former e-hailing driver entrusted with his care.
[[nid:1557202]]
Chan Wen Jie, 32, was sentenced to eight years and six months in prison for abusing the child, who died from his injuries.
In its grounds of judgment, the court described how the boy was forced to eat his own faeces from a diaper, an act it found degrading and unjustifiable.
CCTV footage also showed the child being hit, caned, forced to perform squats and made to stand for prolonged periods.
Chan pleaded guilty to an alternative charge of child abuse after an earlier murder charge was withdrawn. He was convicted and sentenced for abuse.
NAJIB FAILS TO SUSPEND 15-YEAR 1MDB JAIL SENTENCE AND FINE
The Special Corruption High Court dismissed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's application to stay the execution of his 15-year jail sentence and RM11.4 billion fine pending appeal in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) corruption and money laundering case.
[[nid:1557201]]
Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin ruled that Najib had failed to establish special circumstances warranting a stay of execution.
The sentence and fine remain in force unless a higher court orders otherwise.
However, Najib's lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said the decision would not affect his client's eligibility to serve the remainder of his sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.

Title: King graces Royal Mess Night in conjunction with 93rd Armed Forces Day

Title: Trump's new press secretary out after less than week
Article:
WASHINGTON: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was pushed out Friday after less than a week in the high-profile job, following a series of blunders that added to distractions for her embattled boss President Donald Trump.
"Can confirm," a White House official told AFP, after Fox News reported that Zacharia, 41, was "transitioning out."
The writing was on the wall earlier when Trump made clear he was ready to see his newly minted spokeswoman go amid criticism that she had pretended to be a lawyer and over her one, much-mocked press briefing.
"I said, 'Katie, is this for you?'" Trump told reporters. "I said, 'Katie, you don't have to do this'... I said to her, 'Honestly if I were you I'd reconsider.'"
Zacharia only began her job five days ago, taking over from the combative Karoline Leavitt, who helped Trump reshape White House coverage by bringing in more friendly outlets and fiercely attacking critical media.
Zacharia had got off to a rocky start with her debut press room briefing Tuesday morning.
It lasted less than 15 minutes, beginning with a remarkably slow reading out of what she said were Trump's many accomplishments – then taking just three questions from journalists.
She then was plunged into controversy when it emerged that her previous claims to be a lawyer were not true.
The kerfuffle is a distraction for 80-year-old Trump as he flies around the country trying to boost Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 congressional midterm elections, with polls predicting a drubbing.
The Republican leader himself also faces ever-lower polls as Americans sour over the war against Iran, inflation and perceptions of corruption.
NOT A REAL LAWYER
Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.
While she does have a law degree from a California university, she acknowledged Thursday she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.
She embarked on a series of damage-control interviews on Trump-friendly outlets, but they did no good.
In one of them, Fox News' Sean Hannity, a close Trump ally, appeared dismissive of Zacharia.
He asked the press secretary if she ever retook the bar exam. She replied: "I did not."
"It was never my intent to go into the practice of law," she said.
In another interview Thursday with pro-Trump outlet Real America's Voice, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was "distracted and overwhelmed" by plans to move to China with her husband.
Zacharia said "many people in the field" had assured her that she could "label myself a lawyer," given her law degree.
CHINA'S TOILETS
"Fox and Friends," which often conducts friendly interviews with Trump administration officials, was unusually direct Friday when a host asked Zacharia if she still had the confidence of the president.
"I hope to be able to build the trust and confidence of everyone around me," she said, sidestepping the question.
Zacharia further stirred controversy on Thursday when she disparaged China, whose leader Xi Jinping was recently Trump's guest in a pomp-filled Washington visit.
The press secretary recalled the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.
"I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, 'How is China the next country on the horizon? They don't even have proper toilets,'" she told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec in an interview.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning responded Friday that Zacharia should "visit China more often."

Title: 2027 Budget: Record RM57bil financing facilities for MSMEs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has allocated a record RM57 billion in financing facilities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) under the 2027 Budget to help the sector navigate global economic uncertainties.
Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim said the allocation, up from RM50 billion previously, reflected the government's commitment to strengthening the sector through better access to financing, lower business costs and improved government service delivery.
He said the government understood the pressures MSMEs faced amid global economic fluctuations, including rising energy costs and supply chain disruptions beyond the country's control.
"We know that in a time of multiple crises, SMEs must be given breathing space so they can face the various challenges.
"We cannot control energy prices. We cannot control some of the supply chain. At least we can control the ground force here in Malaysia," he said at the Enterprise 50 (E50) Awards ceremony here tonight.
Also present was SME Corp Malaysia chief executive officer Rizal Nainy.
Sim also addressed the latest minimum wage increase, saying MSMEs had been granted an exemption to help ease their operating cost pressures.
However, he stressed that easing the burden on employers did not mean the government was abandoning its goal of creating high-income jobs for Malaysians.
"We all want to see Malaysians secure high-paying jobs, but as the world faces various crises, MSMEs also need to be given space to overcome these challenges," he said.
Sim said MSME performance was a key determinant of the nation's economic growth and expressed optimism that 2027 would be a better year for the sector, supported by government initiatives and the resilience of local entrepreneurs.
Meanwhile, Rizal said the E50 Business Matching programme organised by SME Corp Malaysia had generated RM420 million in potential sales.
He said the two-day programme, held in conjunction with the awards, aimed to expand MSMEs' access to export markets and create new business collaboration opportunities.
"This year's E50 programme took a more meaningful approach. It was expanded with the E50 Export Conference and the E50 Business Matching programme," he said.
Rizal added that the awards received 160 nominations this year, the highest number since their inception in 1997.
He said the increased participation reflected growing recognition of E50 as a platform showcasing the achievements of high-performing Malaysian MSMEs.
At the event, 50 MSMEs received the E50 Award in recognition of their achievements, performance and ability to expand their businesses.
The award recognises excellence in business growth, competitiveness, innovation and governance.

Title: Man critical after homemade fish bomb explodes in Sabah home
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A 37-year-old man is in critical condition after a homemade fish bomb exploded in the kitchen of a house in Kampung Keliangau, Manggatal.
Kota Kinabalu police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said the victim suffered serious injuries to both hands and his abdomen in the 2.15pm incident.
"The victim was taken to Menggatal Health Clinic before being referred to Queen Elizabeth I Hospital (HQEI). He was reported to be in critical condition and unconscious," he said in a statement.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was believed to have been making a homemade explosive device for fishing purposes.
Police, together with the Bomb Disposal Unit from the Sabah police contingent headquarters and officers from the Kota Kinabalu police headquarters inspected the scene.
"During the inspection, several materials suspected of being used to make homemade fish bombs were found and seized for technical examination and further investigation," he said.
Shahrudin said investigations were ongoing to determine the cause of the explosion, the source of the materials used and whether others were involved
The case is investigated under Section 8 of the Explosives Act.

Title: Asked if Trump is scapegoating him, Zelenskyy just smiles
Article:
BRUSSELS: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave a knowing smile and remained silent on Friday when asked if Donald Trump was scapegoating him for troubles in the US.
"This is my answer," Zelenskyy said, as journalists burst into laughter at a press conference in Brussels after he met EU leaders.
Zelenskyy had been asked if Trump was lashing out at the Ukrainian leader to deflect from his own political strife ahead of next month's midterm elections, as he is bogged down by the war in Iran and diesel prices have soared.
The question came after Trump said he found it easier to deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin than with Zelenskyy, as ties with Kyiv have soured.
"Yesterday was a thousand drones in Ukraine, a thousand, but the American side said that it is difficult to speak with Zelenskyy, it's less difficult to manage with Putin," Zelenskyy said.

Title: NST Leader: Scrap metal theft: Go after the buyers, too
Article:
THERE seems to be an almost insatiable demand for scrap metal. And not just locally. It started many years ago.
There was even an international dimension that traced such demand all the way to China. Thus, local councils have been hard put to keep metal covers for manholes and drains in place, among other things.
The raging fire in Pasir Gudang, Johor, in recent days is said to be deliberately started by cable thieves seeking to separate scrap metal from piles of wood. The blaze has spread to an area of 1.4ha. Firefighters were still battling it some 19 hours later.
This is a stark reminder that theft is not merely a property crime when criminals are willing to put lives, the environment and public safety at risk just so they can get their hands on ill-gotten goods.
These cannot be isolated cases. The authorities need to see them for what they are: networks,   organised  syndicates and weak enforcement coming together for such activities to persist.
There is a worrying pattern of recklessness involved here. In recent days, cable thefts have disrupted critical infrastructure, including the KLIA Ekspres and KLIA Transit services.
The common thread is criminals helping themselves to materials for their resale value, with total disregard for the consequences to and convenience and safety of the wider public.
What appears as cost-free quick profit for the thieves will translate into disrupted services, costly repairs and replacements, environmental damage and even risks to human lives.
Any foolproof solutions must target the market for such ill-gotten materials, not just the thieves involved. Enforcement must not stop with arresting those caught stealing.
The authorities must root out the supply chain by identifying and shaming scrap dealers who knowingly purchase stolen materials and take firm action against buyers providing the outlet for such looted goods.
Absent a ready market, the incentive to steal will be substantially reduced. The police, local authorities, government agencies and scrap metal industry players must work together to improve traceability, verify the origins of the materials and single out suspicious transactions.
Licensing and inspection regimens must be consistently enforced, with painful penalties imposed on businesses complicit in facilitating the trade in stolen goods.
Consequences for those caught must be fully proportionate to the harm caused. Investigations into the Johor blaze must establish its cause as well as the extent of responsibility of all those involved.
Where criminal wrongdoing is evident, the prosecution and penalties ought to reflect not only the severity of the crime, but also any additional and related offences and damage caused.
The punishment must be severe enough to act as a deterrent. Punitive certainty and consistency will serve as credible and timely warning to those involved in such sordid and nefarious thefts and trades to desist.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two days on the campaign trail, Trump faces fading enthusiasm
Article:
DONALD  Trump is crisscrossing America to drum up votes for Republican candidates facing tough midterm election races, but the United States president's rallies are often hijacked by his basking in the adulation of fervent supporters.
Journalists followed him on Tuesday and Wednesday during one such trip out West, a rapid succession of flights and rallies — in a glacial valley in Alaska, on an arid plain in Arizona and in the forests of Montana.
The Republican leader is betting on his ability to mobilise voters despite polls predicting that his party will lose control of one or both chambers of Congress on Nov 3.
A
Fox News
poll released on Thursday puts his approval rating at just 36 per cent, a new low, largely because of growing dissatisfaction over the cost of living.
"Please pretend that I am on the ballot," the 80-year-old leader, wearing a red cap, told the crowd Wednesday in Bullhead City, Arizona.
In 2024, he got nearly 78 per cent of the vote in the county where he was speaking in Arizona. The other two counties he visited, in Alaska and Montana, also gave him decisive victories over Democrat Kamala Harris.
Trump makes no secret of his preference for travelling to friendly territory, telling reporters that he wants to "pay my respect" to supporters.
"We brought back the spirit" of the 2024 presidential campaign, he declared. It is difficult to judge.
Each appearance drew committed supporters, the core of his MAGA (Make America Great Again) movement, who are apparently willing to forgive him for soaring fuel prices as well as the war in Iran.
"The country needs to be a little bit more patient," Theresa Hallesy said on Wednesday in Montana.
"There's a lot of stuff going on in the world that he can't control, but he still has to deal with it. I think we're going in the right direction."
The 68-year-old retiree waited more than seven hours for Trump to make his entrance into a large rodeo arena commandeered for the occasion.
The American president is rallying support for his party, but he seemed almost reluctant to invite local candidates to join him onstage during the tour.
"I want you just to come up for one minute because we don't want to hear you for two minutes, three minutes, just one minute," he told Andy Biggs, a conservative seeking to become governor of Arizona.
The Republican leader always has one or two announcements tailored to each region.
In Alaska on Tuesday, at a hockey rink converted into a rally venue, he laid out his climate-sceptic arguments.
In a state whose economy is closely tied to fossil fuels, Trump promoted a major liquefied natural gas project.
He also issued presidential pardons for two auto mechanics who were convicted of modifying diesel engines to circumvent emissions regulations.
At each rally, he  promised that every American will receive US$5,000 if Republicans retain their majorities in the House of Representatives and the Senate.
How this highly controversial proposal, criticised by the opposition, would be funded remains unclear.
Yet rather than an electoral offensive, his rallies give the impression of a final tour for a show whose star performer and audience are already feeling nostalgic.
In Montana, thousands of enthusiastic supporters laughed at a now-familiar impersonation of French President Emmanuel Macron and gave Trump a standing ovation as he left the stage, dancing to the ever-present strains of
YMCA.
In Arizona, the billionaire delighted the audience with a flyover by the new presidential aircraft, a lavish gift from Qatar.
Onstage, he joked about the present, estimated to be worth US$400 million: "You know, when you are given gifts, you take them, right?"
The joke fell somewhat flat with the audience in a district where both the poverty rate and the unemployment rate are significantly above the national average.
The Republican leader then spoke regretfully about the approaching end of his term, saying he has resigned himself to it in "2½ years. Now a little less than that, sadly."
"I said that yesterday and they started screaming, 'Four more years! Four more years!'" Trump continued.
He paused. He waited. The audience eventually took the cue, and a few voices broke into the chant, "Four more years! Four more years!" — without much conviction.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court of Appeal reserves decision in Papagomo's contempt appeal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal three-member panel today reserved its decision on blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris's appeal against the High Court's decision which sentenced him to 30 days in jail for contempt of court in a defamation suit filed by former Inspector-General of Polis Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid.
Justice Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan who chaired the three-member panel fixed Oct 29 for case management to set the date for the decision.
Earlier the panel, also comprising Justices Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun, heard submissions by lawyers representing Azri and Razarudin respectively.
On Aug 27, 2025, High Court Judicial Commissioner Gan Techiong ruled that Azri, also known as Papagomo, had breached a court injunction concerning the ongoing defamation suit filed by Razarudin.
Gan sentenced the blogger to 15 days in jail for failing to properly comply with the court order to apologise to Razarudin, and another 15 days for making a statement in the video which showed a lack of remorse.
The High Court had ordered the custodial sentences to run consecutively and Azri was also ordered to pay Razarudin RM30,000 in costs. However, the court granted Azri a stay of execution of the sentence pending his appeal.
At the hearing of the appeal in the Court of Appeal today, Azri's lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali submitted that his client was not in contempt of court as he had complied with the terms of the court order by reading the agreed unconditional apology to the court and to Razarudin in open court on April 30, 2025 and deleted the earlier publications.
Rafique said Azri had also complied with the court's directive to publish the same apology on his  four social media accounts for at least seven days and had paid RM5,000 in costs as well as his apology was widely reported by the media.
Alternatively, he submitted that jail term imposed on his client should be substituted with a fine.
However, lawyer Raam Kumar representing Razarudin, urged the court to uphold the two contempt orders made by the High Court.
He submitted that Azri failed to genuinely comply with the apology, adding the apology was presented in a manner that made it difficult to read and it was not shown to have been maintained on his relevant social media platforms.
Raam, assisted by Tan Khay Boon and Norleena Jamal further said under Section 69(4) of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964, the court has the power to increase the sentence even if there is no cross-appeal regarding it.
Razarudin filed a RM3 million defamation suit against Azri on Dec 27, 2024 over allegedly defamatory remarks involving him and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
On Jan 10, 2025, Razarudin obtained an injunction prohibiting Azri or his agents from publishing or disseminating defamatory statements about him on social media until disposal of the civil suit.
The High Court had scheduled to hear the contempt of court proceedings initiated by Razarudin on April 30, last year. However, Azri decided to apologise to Razarudin and to the court.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Italy, Spain agree to remove border checks
Article:
BRUSSELS: Italy and Spain have agreed to remove tit-for-tat border checks introduced following a spat over migration, after talks between the two countries' leaders, diplomatic and government sources said on Friday.
The detente ends a showdown that began in summer, when Italy's interior ministry introduced controls on travellers from Spain after tens of thousands of migrants rushed from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta, in North Africa.
Under an agreement reached at an EU summit in Brussels, Rome's measures will remain in place for another week so that they lapse at the same time as Madrid's, according to Italian government sources.
The deal was struck after Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Spain's Pedro Sanchez held talks on the sidelines of the leaders' meeting, where migration was on the agenda, a Spanish diplomat said.
Italy and Spain do not share a land border, but passengers arriving on flights had been required to undergo passport checks, which is not normally the case because both countries are members of the Schengen free-travel zone.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore to issue notices to seven Indonesian firms over haze
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore will issue preventive measure notices to seven Indonesian companies suspected of contributing to transboundary haze through forest fires, Sustainability and Environment Minister Grace Fu said.
She said the notices would be issued by the National Environment Agency (NEA), following investigations into errant companies found responsible for causing transboundary haze in Singapore.
"Our investigation so far suggested that some of the haze experienced in Singapore originated from fires on the lands of seven companies in Indonesia.
"Where warranted, we will take further action under the THPA based on the information and evidence available," she said in a press conference.
Fu said the notices seek the companies to deploy firefighting personnel to extinguish fires on land owned or occupied by them and prevent the fires from spreading.
They are also required to discontinue or not commence any burning activities and submit action plans to the NEA detailing measures to extinguish fires on their land and prevent their recurrence.
Fu also said the haze conditions in Singapore were expected to persist for some time with air quality likely to fluctuate and potentially reach hazardous levels.
"However, as we transit to the inter-monsoon period towards the end of October or early November, we expect the situation to improve and that is another three to four weeks away.
"We expect winds around Singapore to become lighter then and more variable in direction, so it is less likely to bring haze from Sumatra or Kalimantan to Singapore," she added.
As of 7pm on, NEA data showed that the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) had continued to deteriorate with three regions recording very unhealthy air quality.
The 24-hour PSI stood at 225 in the central region, 202 in the west, 201 in the east, 183 in the south and 161 in the north.
Fu said the distribution of N95 masks to vulnerable Singaporeans through 37 vending machines will be fully deployed across the island by Friday night.
On the availability of masks, she assured the public that sufficient mask stocks were available at retailers' warehouses and in government stockpiles.
"The Haze Task Force is working closely with retailers to ensure the availability of masks to the public and we are monitoring the situation and working closely with our partners to ensure that those who need masks can access them," she said.

Title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepts missiles, drones over Riyadh, other areas
Article:
RIYADH: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Friday that it had intercepted missiles and drones over Riyadh and other areas, as the kingdom came under sustained attack from its Iran-backed foes.
Since Yemen's civil war flared up again in July, the Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets, including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.
Saudi Arabia leads a military coalition that has supported Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis for more than a decade.
"We intercepted and destroyed three drones in the southern area and Riyadh... and two cruise missiles over the Red Sea," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki wrote on X.
He added that "in the past hours, we intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile over Yanbu", a city home to the terminus of a major oil pipeline on the Red Sea coast.
The pressure on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, comes as global energy markets were already rattled by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz at the outset of the wider Middle East war in February.
The Houthi attacks have proliferated since the group launched a lightning offensive in Yemen in September, seizing strategic territory held by the government along the Red Sea coast, overlooking a major chokepoint for global shipping.
The UN Security Council on Thursday "condemned in the strongest terms continued and escalatory Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia", as well as their "attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab" Strait, the southern gateway to the Suez Canal.
The Security Council also denounced the group's "reckless strikes" on Riyadh's airport, which the Saudi-led coalition said had been targeted at least 20 times so far this month.
Palace struck
A Saudi foreign ministry official accused Iran on Thursday of continuing "to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN Security Council resolutions".
"We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," said Dr Rayed Krimly, deputy minister for public diplomacy.
Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to retake areas seized by the Houthis, but have so far failed to reverse their gains.
On Thursday, the group launched a deadly missile attack on the presidential palace in Aden, the interim seat of the Yemeni government, killing five people and wounding 16 others, according to the health minister.
Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the "cowardly" act on X, calling it a "continuation of (the Houthis') criminal pattern".
A government minister said on condition of anonymity that Zindani had been present at the time but "was not harmed in any way".
The minister said the Houthis hit a command centre for Yemeni government forces at the complex with three missiles and another for Saudi coalition forces with two missiles.
Media affiliated with the Houthis said they had targeted "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Managing Kuching's thriving private healthcare industry
Article:
THERE is a good reason why after starting off with daily flights from Kuching to Kuala Lumpur and Singapore, the next destination for the Sarawak-owned AirBorneo is Jakarta.
Although AirAsia now flies daily between Kuching and Jakarta, AirBorneo is positioning itself as a premium carrier.
The existing Kuching-Jakarta flights are popular and it is not unusual to see at least a few passengers needing wheelchairs to board and disembark on each flight.
Kuching has successfully tapped into the lucrative Indonesian medical tourism market and the direct flight from Jakarta takes only 1½ hours, making the Sarawak capital the nearest Malaysian city to the Indonesian capital.
The private hospitals in Kuching have for some time already made a name for themselves
with residents from West Kalimantan, and it is believed that Kuching's reputation for reasonably affordable and quality medical care had mostly spread by word-of-mouth to Jakarta residents, from kith and kin in the Borneo province bordering Sarawak.
Such Indonesian medical tourists to Kuching will be even more spoilt for choice as at least two new hospitals are currently under construction.
The 200-bed Gleneagles Hospital Kuching will open in 2028 while the Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching is a 300-bed facility scheduled to open in 2029.
Private healthcare in Kuching was pioneered by the Normah Medical Specialist Centre some 35 years ago.
Three state agencies — the Sarawak Economic Development Corporation, the Sarawak Electricity Supply Corporation and the Sarawak Timber Industry Development Corporation — pooled resources to build this facility.
Since then, two more local private hospitals — Timberland Medical Centre and Borneo Medical Centre — have been set up and are expanding their facilities.
The KPJ Kuching Specialist Hospital rounds up the presently operating four private hospitals in Kuching.
Competition for market share can be expected to go up several notches once the two facilities under construction become operational. It will mean three homegrown establishments vying for clients against three others with  international links.
Normah Medical Specialist Centre, especially, may be ripe for reviewing its setup.
There was a justification for state-led involvement in its establishment decades earlier when the market for private medical centres was untested.
There is less of a reason for it to invest in a new, planned facility if it involves more public funds.
In light of this increased competition, the hospital  should re-examine its strategic position and consider how it will compete in the private healthcare industry of the future.
A comprehensive review of its comparative advantages, service offerings, technological capabilities and long-term growth prospects will be beneficial.
As Sarawak develops further, local demand for private health care can be expected to rise so as to avoid an unhealthy over-dependence on demand from across the border.
It is perhaps an opportune time as well for Normah Medical Specialist Centre and the other private hospitals to explore ways to up their game, such as gaining international accreditation in order to widen the pool of international patients.
The state still has a long way to go as its RM300 million medical tourism revenue a year is only a fraction of the reported RM3.5 billion annual revenue nationally and even pales in comparison with Penang's RM1.5 billion annual take.
* The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ab Rauf: BN's Melaka candidates ready for announcement
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional's (BN) Melaka election candidates have been finalised and could be announced at any time, says state BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
The Melaka chief minister said he would not take long to announce the candidates, with nomination day approaching.
"The entire list of candidates is ready. We will announce it soon... at any time," he said briefly after attending the Sembang Santai Geng E-Hailing dan P-Hailing programme in Kampung Pulau here tonight.
He also dismissed claims that BN's candidates would be announced on Oct 24.
"Who said that (Oct 24)? Ask the person who said it. It did not come from me."
Ab Rauf said BN's preparations were in the final stages, including negotiations with coalition partners to finalise cooperation and the distribution of seats to be contested.
In the 2021 Melaka election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats contested, enabling it to form the state government on its own before Pakatan Harapan (PH) later joined the state administration.
Ab Rauf said the outcome of negotiations with coalition partners would also be announced ahead of nomination day.
"The outcome of the negotiations will be announced after the final round of talks in the near future," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NRD: Viral video of Saifuddin solemnising non-Muslim marriage dates back to 2023
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A viral video showing Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail solemnising a civil marriage between a non-Muslim couple was recorded in 2023, the National Registration Department (NRD) said.
The department said the video was part of its Diamond Jubilee celebration held in conjunction with National Registration Day that year, and the matter had already been clarified on Oct 25 that year.
"NRD takes seriously the recirculation of the video clip of the home minister solemnising a civil marriage between a non-Muslim couple, despite the matter having been officially clarified since Oct 25, 2023.
"Recycling old footage without explaining the actual context, particularly when it creates a misleading perception, is irresponsible and could cause misunderstandings among the public," it said in a statement.
The department said it was responsible for registering civil marriages between non-Muslim couples under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act.
It added that Saifuddin's involvement in solemnising the marriage was part of the department's official programme in 2023 and should be understood in the context of its legal functions.
NRD also said it had sought views from the Federal Territories Mufti Department on relevant aspects of Islamic law.
It said the public to rely on facts and explanations from the relevant authorities rather than assumptions or misleading interpretations.
"Differences of opinion should not be used as a reason to disseminate information out of context and trigger unfounded controversy," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar wishes Malaysian contingent success at Asian Para Games
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has wished the Malaysian contingent success at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games in Japan from Oct 18 to 24.
He expressed hope that the national athletes would demonstrate fighting spirit, courage and determination to give their best at the Games.
"The entire Malaysian people stand firmly behind you. Keep moving forward, achieve success and bring glory to the country!" he said in a Facebook post today.
The national contingent is targeting six gold, 10 silver and 16 bronze medals across athletics, badminton and boccia.
